slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: Lipoprotein lipase (LPL) releases glycerol and free fatty acids from triglycerides; glycerol kinase (GK) with ATP converts glycerol to glycerol-3-phosphate.
Glycerol phosphate oxidase (GPO) forms H2O2; with peroxidase (POD), H2O2, 4-aminophenazone and p-chlorophenol give a red quinone.
The colour intensity is proportional to the triglyceride concentration.

This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “Triglycerides” kit (IFU BSIS31-I, 17/09/20). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum, heparin or EDTA plasma — stable for 5 days at 2–8 °C.
R1 (buffer): GOOD pH 7.5 50 mmol/L, p-chlorophenol 2 mmol/L. R2 (enzymes): LPL 150000 U/L, GK 500 U/L, GPO 2500 U/L, POD 440 U/L, 4-aminophenazone 0.1 mmol/L, ATP 0.1 mmol/L.
Standard: triglycerides 200 mg/dL (aqueous primary standard); LCF is built into the reagent.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 505 nm, 1.0 cm cuvettes.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: Working reagent: dissolve one vial of R2 in one bottle of R1; cap and mix gently.
Working reagent stability: 6 weeks at 2–8 °C or 1 week at room temperature (15–25 °C).

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: Signs of deterioration: particles, turbidity or blank absorbance at 505 nm ≥ 0.14.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The values come from the SPINREACT “Triglycerides” IFU (BSIS31-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 505 nm (490–550); temperature 37 °C or 15–25 °C.
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: blank — working reagent 1.0 mL; standard — working reagent 1.0 mL + standard 10 µL; sample — working reagent 1.0 mL + sample 10 µL.
4. Mix and incubate: 5 min at 37 °C or 10 min at room temperature.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Read the absorbance (A) of the sample and standard against the blank; the colour is stable for at least 30 minutes.

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: triglyceride programme
rows: 5 min at 37 °C or 10 min at room temperature
Sample and standard — against the reagent blank

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: Result (mg/dL) = (A sample − A blank) / (A standard − A blank) × 200 (standard concentration).
Conversion: mg/dL × 0.0113 = mmol/L.
Linear up to 1200 mg/dL; above that, dilute the sample 1/2 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 2.
IFU reference: men 40–160 mg/dL, women 35–135 mg/dL.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Bilirubin up to 170 µmol/L and haemoglobin up to 10 g/L do not interfere.
The standard is easily contaminated — use clean disposable tips.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: IFU: performance depends on the analyser used.

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and calibrator; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
